Hi Leo — thanks for the clear ask. Short summary and next steps below.

What we propose:
- EU residency: Dedicated EU cluster (customer-managed VPC option) with encryption-at-rest + KMS/HSM integration. Data-at-rest and primary KV cache pinned to EU nodes.
- APAC staged burst pilot: 3-month pilot using an APAC burst pool (capacity reserved for pilot, not full dedicated commit). We’ll size for ~30% peak based on your traffic sample.
- SLA & failover: Active-primary in EU; cross-region stand-by failover to APAC with automatic routing and warm standby (we document RTO and RPO in SOW).
- Term: we recommend a 12-month renewal with an upsell addendum for APAC conversion option mid-term.

I’ve attached a draft SOW and an initial pricing worksheet. Highlights: EU dedicated baseline (3 nodes) + APAC pilot pricing and an optional warm-standby add-on if you need <2 minute failover.

Attachments: 2025-06-30_Atlas_SOW_draft.pdf, RDW_pricing_apac_surge.xlsx

If that looks close to what you need I can: 1) lock in a formal SOW (DocuSign link), 2) spin up a pre-prod EU node for compliance testing, and 3) run an internal pricing concession review with Aditya and RevOps.

Available: Tue 6/30 16:00–17:00 BST or Wed 7/1 09:00–11:00 BST for a quick call.

2) Failover behaviour: If EU primary is unavailable, what is the connection moment for APAC? We need an RTO target (preferably <5 minutes) and the expected consistency model during failover.

Hi Leo — answers below and next steps.

KMS/HSM: Yes — we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM in the EU region. Keys can be provisioned in your EU KMS, and our platform will encrypt at-rest using those keys; key material does not leave the EU. I’ve attached the compliance_eu_data_map.pdf with architecture notes and the KMS integration checklist.

Failover: Our standard cross-region failover uses DNS-based routing to a warm standby in APAC. Typical RTO for a warm-standby configuration is 2–6 minutes depending on DNS propagation and hot cache warming. We document the exact RTO/RPO in the SOW; if Atlas needs guaranteed <2 minute failover we can include a warm-standby SLA at an incremental commit (approx +6% of EU commit). Active-active is not part of the standard renewal.

References: I’ve asked our CS team for two short references that recently completed EU residency work; expect an intro by EOD tomorrow.

DocuSign & next steps:
1) DocuSign for the attached SOW: https://www.docusign.net/Signing/?s=RDW-5791-AT
2) Pre-prod EU node for compliance testing — Solutions will schedule a spin-up once we have signed SOW.
3) Pilot kickoff window: week of 7/14 — we’ll confirm exact dates after SOW execution.

Attachments (added): compliance_eu_data_map.pdf

If that all looks good I’ll update pricing per Aditya’s concession and send the DocuSign envelope this afternoon.
